questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Cultural possibilities, i.e. being able to experience the local culture, and how it is to live in Norway like a local.
Possibility of moving there to work in the future.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. All relevant information was provided by the university before arrival and, where relevant, during the stay.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: N/A

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It took quite a long time. Being able to understand Norwegian helped.
I would recommend
hybel.no
and starting the search 6 months prior to arrival

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living off campus is not a problem since it is easy to get around Oslo

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The accommodation provided by the University of Oslo is of a very low standard from what I've seen (the housing in Kringsjå and Sogn, where almost everyone I knew lived) and it is quite far outside the city.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I just sent an e-mail with the couses I wanted, and I was registered with no issues.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could contact the university by email

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesful

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: No advice is needed. Registration was easy

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses is around the same as electives at the University of Copenhagen, perhaps a bit easier

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very little in-class teaching. Only 6 hours per week compared to 12 hours per week at UCPH

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
JUS5310 - EU Competition Law
JUS5680 - Internet Governance
JUS5810 - Opphavsrett

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would strongly recommend EU Competition Law. If you have the motivation to take a course in Norwegian, I would recommend Opphavsrett.

I would not recommend Internet Governance. I found the course very technical and a bit too difficult.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Costs related to cell data. After 2 months I could no longer use the free EU data my Danish cell provider, and I had to switch to a Norwegian one which was much more expensive (I would recommend buying an eSim).

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
More expensive: food, personal spending, cell data
Less expensive: books, transportation, housing

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I know that there were lots of activities available, but I didn't take a closer look as I was already spending all my time on other things

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Trips in the Norwegian nature

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Take trips to Nordmarka or other trips to explore the nature.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Norwegians are extremely welcoming and kind towards Danes

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Live with locals. Don't speak English to locals

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How friendly and inclusive Norwegians are towards Danes

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Learn some basic Norwegian before going, for example on Duolingo
Find accomodation on your own through
hybel.no
so that you can live with Norwegians
Buy basic hiking equipment before going, if you intend to to explore nature, i.e. hiking boots, proper clothing

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply for a lot of grants and mention in the application that you are motivated to explore Norwegian culture (if that is the truth of course) - Norway is expensive and therefore grants will help a lot. There are several grants funding exchange specifically in the Nordics/Scandinavia

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Being able to integrate into the local culture

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Balancing school and free time activities, as I was of course much more motivated to spend time on free time activities during the exchange

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
